blockNote: Title / prologue Start handler (Bank 0B, 772529-772609): waits for Start, then sends the game to the diary menu (scene $FA).

Two actor-defs share one poll loop. sFC_title_start_handler is spawned with sFC_title_intro by scene_event_0CE56D (the title scene $FC list) and first waits $021B frames (539, ~9 s) so the intro's opening seconds cannot be skipped. sFC_actor_0BC9BD polls at once; it is spawned in the actor lists of the four prologue scenes ($8C-$8F, next to pr8C_prologue1/5, pr8D_prologue2, pr8E_prologue3 and pr8F_prologue4), so Start skips the prologue slides as well.

Both variants first mask nearly every button out of joypadCurrent (joypadMaskStd |= $FFFC; vanilla $FFF0, widened by transforms.json) and then poll with COP BranchIfPressed #$1001. In that mask word bit 0 is not a button: it makes the handler test joypadRaw instead of joypadCurrent (see docs/cop/families/input.md, BranchIfPressed), which is how Start ($1000) still gets through the mask. R is not tested.

On Start, TitleToDiaryTransition sets transitionBrightness = 0 and the transition parameters (gfxCacheIdxB = 0: speed 0; gfxCacheIdxA = 1: exit type 1 = instant blank, enter type 0 = graduated fade), queues scene $FA at ($0100,$0370) with COP QueueMapChange, yields one frame, runs one VBlankWaitAndJoypad with DP forced to $0000, and then holds INIDISP = $00 (force blank) every frame until the scene change replaces the actor.

TitleStartDelayedInit: Title-scene variant: suppress the buttons, wait 539 frames, then join the shared poll loop.
TitleStartPollInit: Prologue-scene variant (spawned as sFC_actor_0BC9BD): suppress the buttons and poll immediately.
loc_0BC9C6: Shared poll loop: re-enter every frame; Start (read from joypadRaw) -> TitleToDiaryTransition, otherwise RTL.
TitleToDiaryTransition: Start pressed: reset the transition parameters, queue the change to scene $FA (diary menu) at ($0100,$0370), yield one frame, run one VBlank sync with DP = $0000 (the actor's DP points at its slot, so it is swapped around the call), then keep the screen in force blank until the scene change takes over.

blockNote: HDMA thinker of the world-map travel scene (Bank 03, 239678-239936), spawned by WorldMapController's route-launch phase (COP SpawnThinker). Every frame it builds two per-scanline HDMA tables - one for BGMODE ($2105), one for COLDATA ($2132) - that split the screen at a boundary row and, when a route starts, push that row down the screen. The names with 'sine' or 'window' in this file, and the 'iris' wording in WorldMapController, are historical: no sine table or window register is involved.
=== BUFFERS (double-buffered by frame parity, frameCounter bit 0) ===

Even frames: $7E8800 (BGMODE) and $7E8A00 (COLDATA). Odd frames: $7E8900 (sineTableA) and $7E8B00 (sineTableB). UpdateHdmaWindowParams rebuilds the pair for the current parity and QueueHdmaSineBuffers queues exactly that pair with COP QueueDma. The second operand of QueueDma is the PPU B-bus register ($2100 + #05 = BGMODE, #32 = COLDATA; hdma_channel_config gives each register's transfer mode), not an HDMA channel number.

BGMODE (template binary_03A932 = 7F 07 | 18 07 | 01 09 | 00): 127 lines of $07 (Mode 7), then $18 + offset lines of $07, then one line of $09 (Mode 1 with BG3 priority), then the terminator, which UpdateHdmaWindowParams writes itself. The last value ($09) stays in force below the table, so the screen is Mode 7 down to row 150 + offset and Mode 1 from row 151 + offset.

COLDATA (template binary_03A939 = 7F 00 | 18 00 | 01 FF | 00): the same line counts with data $00 (no colour plane selected = no change), then one line of $FF (all planes, full intensity = white) on the boundary row. Only the first 6 bytes are copied; the bytes after them are what InitSineTableBuffers left in the buffer: the $01FF fill reads as a count byte $FF (repeat mode, 127 lines) followed by data 01, FF, 01, FF, ..., so every other scanline below the boundary gets a white fixed-colour write. The template's seventh byte is never used.
The per-actor offset in $7F2104,X (0 at spawn) is added to the second line count of both tables, so the boundary row moves by one line per offset step.

Spawn: offset := 0, InitSineTableBuffers, then SetEntryHere. Every frame the thinker re-enters at the check below that. While worldMapChoiceId ($0D58) is nonzero and worldMapRouteId ($0D5A) is zero (destination chosen, no route playing yet) it only rebuilds and queues the tables with the current offset. Otherwise (no destination, or a route id is set) it runs the opening sequence once: 2 frames of rebuild + queue, then 40 frames in which the offset grows by 2 per frame (second line count $18 -> $68, boundary row 151 -> 231, i.e. off the bottom of the 224-line screen), then it parks on a final SetEntryHere that keeps rebuilding and queuing with offset 80.
What the strip below the boundary looks like on the world map (and whether it is the intended 'iris') is decoded from the tables, not observed (OQ-I058-1).

HdmaWindowEffect: Thinker entry: offset := 0, InitSineTableBuffers, SetEntryHere; hold the tables at the current offset while a destination is chosen but no route plays; otherwise run the 2-frame hold, the 40-frame offset ramp (+2 per frame) and park (see the block note).
loc_03A85B: Opening sequence: 2 frames of rebuild + queue, 40 frames of offset += 2, then the parked final state.
QueueHdmaSineBuffers: Queue the two tables built this frame with COP QueueDma: even frames $7E8800 -> BGMODE ($2105) and $7E8A00 -> COLDATA ($2132); odd frames $7E8900 and $7E8B00 to the same registers. Each COP takes a direct-table HDMA channel for the next frame.
UpdateHdmaWindowParams: Rebuild both HDMA tables for the buffer chosen by frame parity (Y = $0000 even, $0100 odd, with DBR = $7E): copy template 1 into $8800,Y and template 2 into $8A00,Y, adding the actor's offset ($7F2104,X) to each template's second line count (byte 2), and write the $0000 terminator after the BGMODE table only. The COLDATA table has no terminator; its tail is the fill from InitSineTableBuffers.
loc_03A8BD: Copy both templates into the selected buffer pair.
InitSineTableBuffers: Fill the two COLDATA buffers ($7E8A00 and $7E8B00; the BGMODE buffers are not touched) with 76 words of $01FF, then a $0000 word (DBR = $7E). Not a 'fully open window' (no window register is involved): after the template's first 6 bytes the fill reads as a repeat-mode count byte $FF and data 01, FF, 01, FF, ..., the alternating COLDATA writes below the boundary row. The terminator word is never reached because the screen ends first. Called once at spawn.
loc_03A91A: Fill loop: one $01FF word into each COLDATA buffer per pass, 76 passes.
binary_03A932: BGMODE template: 7F 07 | 18 07 | 01 09 | 00 (line count, value pairs; the final byte is never copied).
binary_03A939: COLDATA template: 7F 00 | 18 00 | 01 FF | 00 (line count, value pairs; the final byte is never copied).
